mechanism: At night, aggregate solar generation is at or near zero and lacks the daytime solar variability signal.
failure_condition: non-zero night values from data errors or non-solar generation; also near dawn/dusk when the night category may not match true sun elevation
retrieval_action: Restrict historical retrieval to night-time windows and do not mix with daytime segments.
expected_effect: The retrieved futures will be near-zero night and early-morning shapes, avoiding daytime variability that would inflate forecast error.
reason: Solar output is physically zero without sunlight, so night segments are nearly deterministic and only other night segments provide relevant baseline behavior.

claim: At night, aggregate solar generation is at or near zero and lacks the daytime solar variability signal.

mechanism: During midday with low volatility and high recent autocorrelation, aggregate solar generation follows a smooth clear-sky curve determined by sun angle and season.
activation_condition: when hour_of_day is midday AND recent_volatility is low AND recent_autocorr is high
failure_condition: when clouds or aerosols create abrupt ramps; when low volatility is only a short calm interval before a front
retrieval_action: Restrict retrieval to midday history and prefer windows with similar recent_level and the same seasonal_level.
expected_effect: Matches the clear-sky baseline amplitude and diurnal shape for the current season and current output level, reducing bias.
reason: Clear-sky solar generation is highly repeatable for a given time of day and season; matching level and season aligns the current clear-sky baseline with analogous past segments.
claim: During midday with low volatility and high recent autocorrelation, aggregate solar generation follows a smooth clear-sky curve determined by sun angle and season.

mechanism: High recent volatility indicates active cloud cover, so the near future is dominated by cloud-driven fluctuations rather than the clear-sky diurnal cycle.
failure_condition: when high volatility is caused by a passing frontal edge that will leave the region within the horizon; also near sunrise/sunset when low sun angle can inflate volatility
retrieval_action: Prefer historical windows with similarly high recent_volatility and large recent_diff_magnitude, and use shorter lags to focus on fast cloud dynamics.
expected_effect: Retrieved futures will contain realistic cloud-induced dips and ramps at similar timescales, reducing bias from clear-sky retrievals.
reason: Cloud cover has persistence and characteristic variability; matching volatility and recent diff magnitude aligns the current cloud regime with analogous past regimes.
claim: High recent volatility indicates active cloud cover, so the near future is dominated by cloud-driven fluctuations rather than the clear-sky diurnal cycle.

mechanism: Morning solar ramp-up creates a steep positive slope; the shape of the ramp depends on sun angle and cloudiness.
activation_condition: when hour_of_day is morning AND recent_slope_magnitude is high
failure_condition: when high slope is due to a cloud edge rather than normal sunrise; when morning ramp is obscured by fog or heavy overcast
retrieval_action: Restrict retrieval to morning history and prefer windows with similar recent_slope_magnitude and recent_level.
expected_effect: Historical morning ramps with similar steepness should provide better forecasts of ramp timing and magnitude over the next hours.
reason: The morning ramp is a semi-deterministic diurnal feature whose slope and level contain information about clear-sky versus cloudy conditions.

mechanism: Evening ramp-down is a steep negative slope dominated by declining sun angle; the shape is repeatable for the same hour and season but cloud edges can distort it.
activation_condition: when hour_of_day is evening AND recent_slope_magnitude is high
failure_condition: when high slope is caused by clearing clouds rather than sunset, or when seasonal sunset time shifts significantly within the broad evening category
retrieval_action: Restrict retrieval to evening history and prefer windows with similar recent_slope_magnitude and recent_level.
expected_effect: Better captures evening decay rate and duration, avoiding morning or midday segments with opposite sign dynamics.
reason: Evening ramp-down is the mirror of the morning ramp but occurs at different sun angles and often with different cloud climatology; same-hour and slope matching improves future decay forecasts.

mechanism: Summer has higher clear-sky capacity and longer day length, so the seasonal baseline level differs markedly from other seasons.
failure_condition: during summer monsoon/cloudy periods or smoke events that make the typical summer clear-sky baseline unrepresentative
retrieval_action: Restrict retrieval to summer historical segments and prefer windows with similar recent_level.
expected_effect: Keeps seasonal sun angle and day length consistent, reducing seasonal bias in the 16-hour future shape.
reason: Solar generation is strongly seasonally dependent; same-season retrievals should produce future diurnal patterns with a compatible daylight envelope.
claim: Summer has higher clear-sky capacity and longer day length, so the seasonal baseline level differs markedly from other seasons.

mechanism: Winter has lower sun angle, shorter days, and lower clear-sky output, so winter segments are most predictive of other winter days.
failure_condition: snow cover may temporarily increase reflected irradiance and make winter segments atypical; very stormy winter periods also fail
retrieval_action: Restrict retrieval to winter historical segments and prefer windows with similar recent_level.
expected_effect: Avoids mixing in high summer generation futures and matches winter daylight length and low sun angle.
reason: Winter solar generation has a distinct diurnal envelope and lower typical level; same-season retrieval reduces seasonal mismatch.
claim: Winter has lower sun angle, shorter days, and lower clear-sky output, so winter segments are most predictive of other winter days.

mechanism: Non-working days may have lower aerosol loading and different aggregate demand or curtailment, leading to slightly different solar generation levels or shapes.
failure_condition: when large-scale weather changes dominate the day-type effect; or if the solar fleet is mostly utility-scale and insensitive to weekly activity
retrieval_action: Prefer historical non-working-day windows with similar recent_level and recent_volatility instead of mixing workdays and non-working days.
expected_effect: Retrieves futures with the same weekly atmospheric and operational signature, improving daily level and ramp timing.
reason: Weekly cycles in aerosols, cloud condensation nuclei, or grid operations can modulate aggregate solar output; matching day type may remove a systematic day-of-week bias.
claim: Non-working days may have lower aerosol loading and different aggregate demand or curtailment, leading to slightly different solar generation levels or shapes.
